clue.text: Which camouflaged soldiers ardently seek hideout, sounding rough?

parts.note: to woo is to court someone ardently
a den is a lair or hideout

indicators.note: sounding asks for a word that sounds like the one for rough, spelt differently

parts.note: a rough voice is hoarse

explanation.surface: A question about a lovesick fugitive with a rasping voice hunting for a place to hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' tells you to swap HOARSE for the word that sounds the same but is spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greeks hid soldiers inside the Trojan wooden horse, so it is the thing that concealed them.

clue.text: Sweatin' regularly, half-kilo repeatedly shed somewhere in Pacific

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the word Sweatin', starting from the second
repeatedly asks for the half-word piece to be written twice
half-kilo, with the rest shed, keeps only the first two letters of kilo

explanation.surface: Someone sweating off a half-kilo again and again, perhaps on a Pacific holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' backs up 'half': the second half of kilo is shed each time, leaving KI twice. 'regularly' gives WAI from the even letters of Sweatin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Waikiki is a famous beach district of Honolulu, Hawaii, out in the Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Animal definitely spat out plant

parts.note: an ox is a farm animal

indicators.note: spat out means said out loud, so the word for definitely is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: aye is a dialect word for yes, definitely

explanation.surface: A creature indignantly spitting out a plant it was given to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxeye daisy is a common wild flower of meadows and verges.

clue.text: One's admitted tirade supporting hospital department

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes second

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: A patient who ranted at hospital staff gets admitted all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's admitted' means 'one who is admitted', the person let in.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrant is someone who enters or is let into a place or competition.

clue.text: Bob perhaps broadcast Latin number in booth

indicators.note: in places the broadcast and number pieces within the booth word

parts.note: a hut is a small booth or shed
to air a programme is to broadcast it
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone called Bob broadcasting a Latin number from a booth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; it is the short hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is one style of trimmed hair, an example of what a barber or stylist gives.

clue.text: 3-D chart to remain in warped frame on piano

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the piano letter comes last
in sets the remain word inside the warped frame letters
warped says the letters of frame are bent out of order

parts.note: to lie is to remain, as land lies fallow
p is the musical marking for piano, soft

explanation.surface: Instructions for leaving a three-dimensional chart in a buckled frame resting on a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warped' rearranges the frame letters as REFMA, and 'in' slots the remain word into it after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief map shows hills and valleys by raised modelling, giving a three-dimensional chart.

clue.text: One hears tale by Harrow's third or fourth former

indicators.note: this word only joins the neighbouring pieces: it says which one stands next to which in the answer

parts.note: the ear is the organ one hears with
a lie is a tall tale

indicators.note: the third letter of Harrow and its fourth are the same, so either picks it

explanation.surface: A former Harrow pupil recalls hearing a tale, third or fourth in the school.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English public school, whose pupils are 'formers'; 'former' is in fact the definition. Its third and fourth letters are both R.
explanation.definitionFit: Former and earlier are synonyms describing something that came before.

clue.text: Food illness making two bits go the wrong way

indicators.text: two bits go the wrong way
indicators.note: two neighbouring letters of the illness word swap places, as if going the wrong way round

parts.note: an ailment is an illness

explanation.surface: Bad food causing an illness that makes things go down the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the second and third letters of AILMENT gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for nourishment or sustenance.

clue.text: At Boxing Day, there's commotion following dodgy sherry

indicators.note: following puts the commotion piece after the dodgy one
boxing means enclosing, so At wraps around the day

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday
dodgy can mean ill or unwell
ado is fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: A fuss on Boxing Day after somebody drinks some dubious sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing Day' looks like the 26th December holiday; 'Boxing' is the container signal instead, and Day is shortened as on a calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: Amontillado is a type of Spanish sherry, darker than fino.

clue.text: Heading from highland, look over ancient territory

indicators.note: heading from means the leading letter is taken off

parts.note: highland country is hilly

indicators.note: over means turned over, read backwards

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: A walker leaving the highlands to survey an ancient land.
explanation.definitionFit: Illyria was an ancient region on the eastern Adriatic coast, in the Balkans.

clue.text: Transform son, being dragged inside amusement park

indicators.note: inside puts the being dragged pieces within the transform-plus-son letters

parts.note: to alter is to transform
on can mean taking place, being
on tow means being pulled; tow means dragged

explanation.surface: A boy being changed after being dragged along to a theme park.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a large theme park in Staffordshire, England. 'being dragged' reads as the phrase 'on tow'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the best-known theme park in Britain, with rollercoasters and rides.

clue.text: Postponed recall of some exec in office

indicators.note: recall says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A deferred recall of an executive's work in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: ECINO is found inside 'exec in office' and read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans put on hold are said to be kept in cold storage, a common idiom for deferral.

clue.text: Scientific pioneer, 50, appearing in long film

indicators.note: appearing in puts the fifty letter inside the long word

parts.note: to ache for something is to long for it
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a mist is a thin film, as on glass

explanation.surface: A fifty-year-old scientist cast in a lengthy movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long film' looks like a feature-length movie; long is the verb ACHE and film is MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Alchemists, seeking to turn base metal into gold, were forerunners of modern chemistry.

clue.text: Clown catches nose removing old clothes

indicators.note: catches means holds inside, so the clown word wraps the rest

parts.note: a twit is a fool or clown

indicators.note: removing takes the old letter out of nose

explanation.surface: A clown grabs a red nose after shedding his old costume.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinset is a matching cardigan and jumper, a set of garments worn together.

clue.text: Stuffing's knocked out of servant bearing luggage for flight

indicators.note: removing the stuffing leaves only the outside letters of servant

parts.note: air is a bearing or manner
a case is a piece of luggage

explanation.surface: A porter carrying cases for a flight gets the stuffing knocked out of him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like air travel, in keeping with luggage; it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is a run of steps, one stretch of the climb between floors.

clue.text: Primate and a member of the flock reflected, breaking bread

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open the bread word to go inside

parts.note: a tin is a tin loaf of bread

indicators.note: reflected means mirrored, so the flock member's word is read backwards

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, one of a flock

explanation.surface: A monkey and a sheep share a loaf, seen in a mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' gives MAR, and a tin loaf is the bread being broken open.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamarins are small South American monkeys, a kind of primate.

clue.text: Oriental leaves China, moving back north during depression

indicators.note: moving back means read in reverse

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate, from china plate; pal means mate

indicators.note: during sets the north letter inside the depression word

parts.note: a sag is a dip or depression

explanation.surface: A traveller leaves China and heads back north in low spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; it is Cockney rhyming slang for a mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapsang souchong is a smoky Chinese black tea, so it comes from tea leaves of the East.

clue.text: Bakery food hampers supplied with a little butter

parts.note: a pat is a small portion of butter
ties can mean restricts or hampers

explanation.surface: Hampers of baked goods delivered with a little butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hampers' looks like picnic baskets; it is the verb, ties.
explanation.definitionFit: Patties are small pies or cakes of minced meat or pastry, food sold at bakeries.

clue.text: Lustful place in India, joining hot model in retreat

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so these letters reverse

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
to sit is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: A lusty trip to an Indian resort with an attractive model on a retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Goats are traditionally symbols of lechery, so a goatish person is lecherous.

clue.text: One house member is driven to husband's shed to get painting

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals
an MP is a member of the House of Commons

indicators.note: shed means cast off, so the husband letter is dropped

parts.note: someone driven to do something has to do it
h is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: An MP is forced to take refuge in her husband's garden shed to paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden hut; it means cast off, removing H from HAS TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is a painting technique where the paint is laid on thickly.

clue.text: Brutal throbbing advanced, nursed by local

indicators.note: nursed by means held inside the local word

parts.note: a local is the neighbourhood pub, an inn
a hum is a steady throbbing sound
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: A throbbing hangover, nursed down at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' is British slang for one's nearest pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhuman and brutal both describe cruelty lacking compassion.

clue.text: Son replaces front of portable accessory that checks tide

indicators.note: replaces front of means the opening letter is swapped for the son letter

parts.note: a handbag is a carried accessory

explanation.surface: A son swapping his mother's bag for gear that holds back the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacks filled with sand are piled into walls to hold back floodwater and high tides.

clue.text: When American class gets history or geography results?

definitions.text: When American class gets history or geography
definitions.meaning: in US schools maths is math, and history or geography is the lesson that comes next
the consequences that follow an event

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about results in an American school timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it says 'after math', when the next class comes along.
explanation.definitionFit: The aftermath of an event is its consequences, especially unpleasant ones.

clue.text: Take a breather before beginning to erect some fencing

indicators.note: before places the breather ahead of the next letter

parts.note: a lung is the organ that breathes, a breather

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the opening letter of erect

explanation.surface: Pausing for breath before starting to put up a garden fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' looks like garden panels; it is the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a thrusting attack in swordplay, one move in the sport.

clue.text: Fast intro to intense musical passages

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

indicators.note: intro to asks for the opening letter of intense

explanation.surface: A quick introduction to some intense music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like an adjective for tempo; it is the period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenti is the plural of lento, a slow passage of music.

clue.text: Artistic trade folded in Manila?

parts.note: looks like an art business closing in the Philippine capital, but manila is also a kind of paper, and this craft is folded paper

explanation.surface: A report that an arts business in the Philippine capital has gone under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'folded' suggests a failed business; it is literal folding of manila paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese craft of folding paper into figures, which might use manila sheets.

clue.text: Vehicle skirts round middle of suburb

indicators.note: round means the skirts word goes around the next piece

parts.note: minis are short skirts

indicators.note: middle of asks for the central letters of suburb

explanation.surface: A van that drives round the edges and middle of a suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' looks like a verb, edging round; it is the noun, minis.
explanation.definitionFit: A minibus is a small bus, a vehicle for a dozen or so passengers.

clue.text: One lays piece on part of staircase for scary plot architect

indicators.note: on means placed after the staircase piece

parts.note: a step is part of a staircase
a hen is one that lays eggs
the king is a chess piece

explanation.surface: Someone laying a chess piece on a stair, like a scheme in a horror novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen King is the American horror novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: He is a writer famous for horror novels, someone who constructs frightening stories.
